newsitem.title: JAPAN: All Tokyo corn futures end higher on strong dollar.
newsitem.headline: All Tokyo corn futures end higher on strong dollar.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures ended higher across the board on Wednesday as the dollar's sharp gains against the yen triggered active buying, traders said.
Prices were 20 to 100 yen higher, with the most active Janaury 1998 contract was up 100 yen at 15,690 yen per tonne. The day's volume was 152,401 lots.
The dollar soared to 122.75 yen during Tokyo trading, its highest level in almost four years.
"The dollar's gains offset the Chicago market's weak mood overnight, and encouraged local investors to start buying actively," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot March contract on the CBOT Project A trading system was being traded at $2.74-1/4 per bushel at 0815 GMT, against $2.74-3/4 at Tuesday's close.
The spot March of the CBOT soybean futures on the overnight trading system was at $7.43-1/2 at 0815 GMT, down from $7.44-1/2 at Tuesday's close.
